item.title: Bridging the Beat presents "Go-Go Live AVL" — Sat Aug 8, 7:00 PM — YMI Cultural Center/Pack Square Park
item.description:
Experience the energy, culture, and history of Go-Go—the official music of Washington, D.C.—during an unforgettable weekend in Asheville! Join us for Bridging the Beat, a dynamic celebration featuring lectures, community conversations, visual art, dance exhibitions, youth programming, DJs, delicious food, and fellowship. Whether you’re discovering Go-Go for the first time or you’ve been rocking to the beat for years, this weekend offers something for everyone. Led by Sekou Coleman, Bridging the Beat is a collaborative initiative presented in partnership with the YMI Cultural Center and a network of community partners committed to preserving and celebrating Black cultural traditions. Come learn the history, feel the rhythm, and Beat Ya Feet in AVL as the unmistakable sound of Washington, D.C., takes over Asheville for one incredible weekend!
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: COMING Saturday August 15 | Dirty Logic: A Steely Dan Tribute — Sun Aug 9 — Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain
item.description:
Saturday, August 15 | Show: 7:30 pm | Outdoor Stage | $36.15 adv. Event Details and Tickets Dirty Logic will be performing at Pisgah Brewing Company on Friday, August 15 for a full evening of Steely Dan classics—set against the backdrop of one of Western North Carolina’s favorite outdoor stages. Bring a lawn chair, settle in, and make an evening of it!
This 11-piece band draws from some of Asheville’s finest musicians, united by a shared love and deep reverence for the Steely Dan songbook. What you’ll hear is more than faithful reproduction—it’s a heartfelt celebration of one of the most sophisticated and enduring catalogs in American music. The iconic hits, the deep cuts, the intricate solos, and the funkier live arrangements that longtime fans treasure.
Every show is both a careful honoring of the studio recordings and a living, breathing musical experience—the kind that reminds you why this music has stayed with people for decades.

item.title: SUNDAY EVENING | New Amsterdam String Band — Sun Aug 9 — Asheville Art Museum
item.description:
Sunday, August 9, 2026 | 6:30 pm – 8:30 pm
$22 for Members; $25 for non-members click here!
The New Amsterdam String Band is a dynamic NYC-based ensemble of Juilliard-trained musicians. The concert features connections between American fiddle traditions and their European roots and includes a discussion of two artworks related to the music.
New Amsterdam String Band unites virtuosity, fiddling, and improvisation. Founded while still students at The Juilliard School, NASB finds its roots in historic string playing combined with New York City energy. The ensemble has performed with Rhiannon Giddens and Paul Simon, and recently recorded for an upcoming PBS documentary, produced by Ken Burns. New Amsterdam String Band’s members are Jimmy Drancsak, Lydia Becker, Graham Cohen, Nathan Francisco, and Logan Zaud.

item.title: Block Printing on Fabric — Fri Aug 28, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Block Printing on Fabric with Erika Busse Friday, August 28 | 1 – 3 pm Register Here!
In this 2-hour course, Erika will teach you how to make a relief block and print it from start to finish. This is a great intro course for anyone looking to learn more about printmaking or for a fun experience with art to take home. Relief printing is a reduction process, carving out an image onto a stamp. Erika will teach you how to make a design, transfer it to the block, and how to carve it. Then you will get to print your block onto tea towels with her guidance. You will make a unique work of art and get to take home your tea towel and block. Erika Busse is a full-time artist in Asheville, NC, working to bring joy and whimsy back to life through art making. Deeply inspired by the Appalachian Mountains, she makes printmaking and paintings inspired by it, connecting her to others who share this love for nature. She moved to Asheville after graduating from the University of Alabama in 2017 to

item.title: Wool Spinning Demonstration with Jamie Sparks — Sat Sep 5, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with more than 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the southeastern U.S., including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils. Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.
Source: Asheville Art Museum

**Sundays 8/16-9/13, 10:30am-11:45am** Whether it’s everyday stress, sadness, or even anger, our suffering can be transformed into inner strength, love, and joy. The first step is understanding its source. In this series, we’ll explore Buddha’s teachings on the Four Noble Truths. The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddhist thought and gives us a clear, precise way to understand our life and how to move forward in it. Through teachings and meditation, we’ll discover that suffering comes not from external conditions, but from our own mind. Recognizing this opens the door to transforming our experience and uncovering a more lasting, genuine happiness. item.title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND — Sat Oct 3, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.
Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.
The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.
Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!
